content: SQLAlchemy 2.0 async (AsyncEngine/AsyncSession) supports with_for_update() which appends FOR UPDATE and works on PostgreSQL (true row lock, supports nowait/skip_locked). SQLite does NOT support SELECT FOR UPDATE at all -- it has no row-level locking, only whole-database file locking (SHARED/RESERVED/EXCLUSIVED). The portable pattern for one SQL impl spanning both: use BEGIN IMMEDIATE (acquires the write/RESERVED lock upfront on SQLite, equivalent effect to FOR UPDATE for a single-writer engine) combined with a dialect check -- issue with_for_update() only on Postgres, and rely on BEGIN IMMEDIATE (via connection execution_options or engine event listener) on SQLite to get equivalent serialization. Current SQLAlchemy 2.0.x stable is 2.0.52 (Aug 2026); 2.1 is in RC. Use asyncpg as the Postgres async driver, aiosqlite as the SQLite async driver.
